output.brief:
The departures are concentrated on one matter. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel resigned, against 1 of the 13 who were never on it. Other groups are stable, and the billable-target rise applied to all of them. That makes pay, the target change and ordinary market movement poor explanations. Pay didn't differ for the one associate who left from outside Kestrel, and the rise in the target hit every group. Kestrel associates also record far heavier hours (2,270 a year against 1,940 for the rest of the group) and far more weekend work. The survey comments point to both overwork and humiliating treatment from the supervising partner. I can't separate those two. All 11 Kestrel associates report to Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no one else, so workload and supervision are completely entangled. I'm moderately sure the cause sits in Kestrel (workload plus supervision), but I can't say how much each part contributes.

Next steps: don't pay the retention payment or close the review. Commission the confidential external interviews (about £9k, three weeks), structured to separate supervision from workload. Meanwhile, consider low-cost reversible steps such as reducing weekend load. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Decide on moving supervision or hiring contract reviewers once the interviews are in.
